pairs.difference: A (gold pan): the rim has crisp, even double edges, and the nuggets and water ripples have light, broken internal lines. The outer edge is clean, with no drawn contour. B (oil lamp): the brass base and foot carry several heavy, evenly dark bands, and the chimney has a continuous dark contour of the same weight all the way round. That uniform outline weight matches the generated cards in the lessons. The measured values for both cards fall inside the real range, so this is only a lean.
pairs.fix: Separate the lamp from the background with light and colour change only. Draw no dark contour line around the glass chimney or the brass base. Make edges softer on the base and sharper only at the flame and the glass rim.

pairs.difference: A (harmonica): many small hard edges at the comb holes and screws. Subject edge density is 0.163, just above the real range, but every line is thin and tied to a real part. B (folding fan): a thick, even, dark line runs around the whole top arc and the outer pleats, like an inked outline. The pleat seams inside are thin by comparison. The heavy perimeter is the generated tell.
pairs.fix: Draw no dark line around the fan's outer edge. Let the purple paper end against the yellow background with a clean colour edge. Keep the pleat folds as soft shading changes, not drawn lines.

pairs.difference: A (cowboy hat): a crisp silhouette with a soft felt interior and very few internal edges. Outline darkness is low (-0.136), with no drawn contour. B (scout jacket): every badge, pocket flap, button, collar and the sash border carries a dark, even stroke. The many hard internal seams make the subject look inked; subject density is 0.159, at the top of the real range.
pairs.fix: Outline the badges, pockets and sash only with shading, never with dark lines. Keep seams as thin, faint creases. Leave the large fabric areas smooth, with few internal edges.

pairs.difference: A (gas pump): the dial, counter, nozzle and base all have dark, even contours, and the desert mesas behind carry many edges of their own. Background detail competes with the subject. B (buoy bell): smooth forms with soft, lost edges on the red body. Only the bell and the water ripples carry hard edges. Its hierarchy is closer to the real cards.
pairs.fix: Blur and simplify the desert mesas into soft shapes with no edge detail. Remove the dark line around the pump body and dial. Keep the sharpest edges on the gauge and the nozzle only.

pairs.difference: A (popcorn cart): the awning, wheels and glass have clean, thin edges, and the paving behind is light. B (saddle on hay bale): the hay is a field of hundreds of hard strand edges, giving background edge density 0.076, far above the real maximum of 0.046. The leather also carries dotted stitch lines on every panel edge. The edge density everywhere competes with the saddle.
pairs.fix: Paint the hay bale as smooth, soft golden masses with only a few large straw clumps, not individual strands. Reduce the stitching to one subtle seam. Make the saddle the area with the sharpest edges.

pairs.difference: A (rocking chair): clean silhouette with thin plank seams, and the floor boards have simple lines. B (barrel): wood-grain streaks inside every stave, dark rings around the iron hoops, and a speckled dirt floor of scattered tiny edges. This matches the generated computer lessons, where wood grain and floor texture filled the background with noise.
pairs.fix: Draw the barrel staves as smooth painted wood with no grain streaks. Make the ground a flat, soft-shaded surface with no pebbles or speckles. Make the hoops show as bands of light and shadow, not dark outlined rings.

pairs.difference: Both subjects are dense, with A at 0.234 and B at 0.227, at or just above the real maximum. A (cowboy boots): the density comes from the dotted stitch patterns, and the silhouette has no outline. B (sneakers): a thick dark contour runs round both soles and uppers, the mesh panels are a noisy dot texture, and a hard horizon line cuts behind them.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark contour around the sneakers and their soles. Show the mesh as a smooth colour area with a faint pattern. Fade the wall–floor horizon into a soft gradient.

pairs.difference: A (cactus): soft ribs, small spine edges, and a silhouette that softens against the sand. Outline darkness is -0.037. B (spring-rider duck): one heavy, even dark contour wraps the entire duck body, head and wing, like a sticker outline. Outline darkness is 0.078, and the interior is nearly edgeless.
pairs.fix: Separate the duck from the green background by its own yellow-to-orange shading, with no dark outline. Keep the sharpest edges on the eye, beak and handle.

pairs.difference: A (fountain): thin, precise rim and tier edges, and the paving lines in the background are light. B (covered wagon): outline darkness is 0.158, above the real maximum of 0.097. Heavy dark rings outline the wheels, the canvas hoops and the bed. The canvas has wrinkle noise and the dirt is covered in speckles.
pairs.fix: Draw no dark lines around the wheels and canvas. Shape them with light and shadow. Make the dirt ground smooth and plain, without pebbles, and keep the canvas folds as a few soft, broad creases.

pairs.difference: B is the real lighthouse card, with thin brick seams and soft clouds. A (windmill): subject edge density is 0.333, well above the real maximum of 0.270. Every blade, strut and stone block has a hard edge. The grass tufts and ground add many edges in the background, and the clouds have drawn scalloped contours.
pairs.fix: Simplify the windmill wheel to fewer, broader blades and the tower to a few thick beams. Paint the grass as soft colour patches, not individual blades. Draw no contour lines around the clouds.

pairs.difference: A (campfire): subject edge density is low (0.079), but the rocks, teapot and ground are covered in stippled noise. Cabin logs, pine trees and grass tufts add drawn edges across the whole background, so there is no clear focus. B (viewer binoculars): bold, even contours on the viewer, and the skyline has many window lines. Its focus stays on the lenses.
pairs.fix: Paint the rocks and teapot as smooth surfaces with no speckle texture. Blur the cabin and trees into soft dark shapes without edges. Put the sharpest edges only on the logs and the teapot rim.

pairs.difference: A (neck pillow): subject edge density is 0.017, far below the real minimum of 0.046. The surface is a mesh of fine crinkle texture with no structural seams. A single heavy dark line traces the inner hole and the lower outer edge, unlike any real card. B (water bottle): clean, thin, precise edges on the cap, loop and grip curve, with a crisp silhouette.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line around the inner hole and the outer edge of the pillow. Give it a few clear, thin seam lines and smooth plush shading instead of fine wrinkle texture.

pattern: Generated cards show themselves on this vector in two ways. First, an even, dark contour around the subject or its parts, like an inked outline (duck, wagon wheels, fan edge, jacket badges, pillow hole). Second, edge noise spread where real cards stay quiet: wood grain, speckled dirt floors, hay strands, grass tufts, fabric crinkle. On real cards the subject is set apart by light and colour change, internal seams are thin and few, and the background is nearly edgeless.
